items.title: David Spinozza interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, NY, September 27, 2025
items.q: And that’s the first time I heard those guys play. And I obviously could keep up and everybody liked me... the rhythm section was Chuck Rainey, Bernard Purdie, Richard T, and me.

ctx.x: How – why? Why did people know your name to have you do that?

I think what happened was, one of my friends growing up was Tommy Mottola, who became the president of CBS/Columbia. But at the time he wanted to be a singer, like a Fabian or one of those “good hair” guys, you know, that sang. And he was doing a demo for a company and he said, and he wanted me to play on the record. And there was an arranger named Horace Ott, who went on to produce YMCA and all that stuff. He was an R&B arranger. But he was doing the arrangements I think, for Tommy. Tommy was © Fillius Jazz…

doing the session. Tommy said, “Do you mind if I bring my friend David in to play the guitar?” And Horace said, “Well as long as he can keep up because he’s going to be playing with session musicians and if he can keep up it’s okay but if not, -- you know.” So I went to the session and the rhythm section was Chuck Rainey, Bernard Purdie, Richard T, and me.
